items.answer: Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

A virtual reality system is a system that presents a computer-generated artificial environment, provides computer-generated sensory stimuli for an immersive experience, and lets the user's actions partially determine what happens in it.

A head-mounted display (HMD) is a wearable, mobile visual display that integrates electronic, optical, mechanical, and audio components and uses one or two small screens directly in front of the user's eyes to place images for monoscopic or stereoscopic viewing. It can be non-see-through, optical see-through, or video see-through.
Stereoscopic vision is the perception of three-dimensional objects and space from left and right two-dimensional images processed simultaneously, aided by binocular vision.

items.prompt: What is non-immersive virtual reality system?
items.answer: A non-immersive virtual reality system is a limited class of computer application that provides a computer-generated environment in which a user controls characters or activities while retaining control of the physical environment. The user is psychologically engaged and remains physically attached to the real world, while the virtual environment does not directly interact with the user.

questions.question: Cybersickness is primarily relevant to which immersive technology?
options: Augmented reality
Virtual reality
Extended reality
Mixed reality
questions.explanation: Cybersickness, also called visually induced motion sickness, is a condition that can affect people during interaction with virtual reality and is primarily relevant to VR.

questions.question: If a person reports nausea, dizziness, or dryness of mouth during a VR experience, what can be assumed?
options: Sensory overload may be happening or going to happen
Headset failure may be happening or going to happen
Motion sickness may be happening or going to happen
Cybersickness may be happening or going to happen
questions.explanation: Common symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, or dryness of mouth during VR can indicate that cybersickness is present or starting. Motion sickness may be related, but the indicated condition is cybersickness.

questions.question: Why does lowering the impact of cybersickness matter for virtual reality systems?
options: It can improve user experience and broaden appeal to more people
It can shorten development time and broaden appeal to more people
It can increase tracking accuracy and broaden appeal to more people
It can reduce hardware cost and broaden appeal to more people
questions.explanation: Reducing cybersickness is important because it greatly enhances overall user experience and makes VR applications more appealing to a wider range of people, not because it directly reduces cost, improves tracking, or speeds development.

data.text: Cybersickness, also called visually induced motion sickness, is a condition that can affect people using VR. Recognizable symptoms can show that it is occurring or about to occur, and it can result from many factors rather than one. Reducing cybersickness is important for VR usability and acceptability because it improves the overall user experience and makes VR applications more appealing to a wider range of people.
points: Cybersickness, also called visually induced motion sickness, can occur during VR interaction and is primarily relevant to VR.
One or more symptoms, like nausea, dizziness, vomiting, fatigue, or disorientation, can signal cybersickness onset or occurrence in VR.
Cybersickness can be caused by many factors, not by a single factor.
Reducing cybersickness matters for VR usability and acceptability because it improves overall user experience and broadens appeal.

questions.question: Which of these is an internal factor in the causes of cybersickness?
options: The design of the virtual reality content
The latency of the virtual display
The resolution of the head-mounted display
A user's susceptibility to motion sickness
questions.explanation: Cybersickness causes are divided into internal user-related factors and external factors; external factors include hardware and VR content, while motion-sickness susceptibility is an individual user characteristic.

questions.question: How can prior or repeated exposure to VR affect the link between motion sickness susceptibility and cybersickness?
options: It can strengthen that link and increase cybersickness severity over time
It can mask that link by hiding the user's motion sickness susceptibility over time
It can shift that link from an internal factor to an external hardware factor over time
It can weaken that link and reduce cybersickness severity over time
questions.explanation: Motion sickness susceptibility and cybersickness risk are positively related, but prior or repeated VR exposure can reduce that effect and reduce severity over time, so the link may not hold once exposure is present.

questions.question: How does the relationship between age and cybersickness differ for general VR content compared with controllable VR content?
options: Age may be equally clear for general content and controllable content
Age may be clearer for general content and less clear for controllable content
Age may be less clear for general content and clearer for controllable content
Age may be irrelevant for general content and decisive for controllable content
questions.explanation: Age can be independent of cybersickness when users view general VR content, but it can become a clearer factor when the content is controllable, making the age relationship more evident in that setting.

questions.question: Which emotional state while using VR is typically associated with a higher likelihood of cybersickness?
options: Confidence, relaxation, or enjoyment
Boredom, surprise, or curiosity
Anxiety, stress, or frustration
Hunger, thirst, or fatigue
questions.explanation: Negative emotional conditions at the time of use, such as anxiety, stress, and frustration, can increase the likelihood of cybersickness, while the other listed states are not given as typical risk factors.

data.text: Cyber sickness in VR can be understood by separating its causes into internal user factors and external hardware or content factors. Internal factors include age, gender, motion sickness susceptibility, physical condition, and emotional condition, which can all shape susceptibility. Age and gender effects are qualified by content type, evidence, and fit issues, while motion sickness, physical, and emotional factors may increase risk but repeated VR exposure can reduce it.
points: Cyber sickness is studied through causes, evaluation, and mitigation; causes are internal or external hardware and VR content.
Internal factors for cybersickness are age, gender, motion sickness susceptibility, physical condition, and emotional condition.
Age may affect cybersickness susceptibility, especially for controllable content, and it is highly unlikely from age 12 to 25.
Gender findings are inconclusive, but female HMD use may increase cybersickness, possibly due to poorer IPD fit.
Motion sickness susceptibility, physical conditions, and emotional conditions can increase cybersickness, but prior VR exposure may reduce it.

questions.question: What does it show that cybersickness can persist in advanced VR systems?
options: that advanced hardware shifted the cause to user susceptibility
that advanced hardware shifted the cause to the virtual environment
that inferior hardware quality still explains the symptoms in advanced systems
that some aspects of the devices themselves induce it
questions.explanation: Cybersickness is not only a sign of poor hardware; some properties of VR devices can themselves induce it, so it can remain even in advanced systems.

questions.question: In VR display-resolution comparisons across 1K, 2K, 3K, and 4K, how does cybersickness induction change as resolution increases?
options: It drops substantially from 1K to 2K, then changes little afterward
It changes little from 1K to 2K, then drops substantially afterward
It rises from 1K to 2K, then drops substantially afterward
It drops gradually from 1K to 4K, then changes little afterward
questions.explanation: Higher resolution reduces cybersickness mainly up to a point: the large improvement is from 1K to 2K, with no significant further reduction from 2K to higher resolutions.

questions.question: How do latency and latency jitter differ in HMD-based VR?
options: latency is resolution, while jitter is brightness
latency is a delay, while jitter is variability
latency is input method, while jitter is display type
latency is variability, while jitter is a delay
questions.explanation: Latency is the time gap between a physical movement and its virtual reflection; latency jitter is the variation in that time gap over time.

questions.question: How does display type relate to the severity of cybersickness when stereoscopic 3D content is viewed?
options: non-immersive VR systems are associated with more cybersickness than HMD displays
panoramic screens are associated with more cybersickness than HMD displays
flat screens are associated with more cybersickness than HMD displays
HMD displays are associated with more cybersickness than flat or panoramic screens
questions.explanation: Display type matters: HMD or VR headset displays are associated with more cybersickness than conventional or non-immersive display types such as flat or panoramic screens.

questions.question: How can the choice of input method affect the level of cybersickness in VR?
options: motion controls can cause more cybersickness than non-motion controls
gamepad controls can cause more cybersickness than hand controls
handlebar controls can cause less cybersickness than joystick controls
non-motion controls can cause more cybersickness than motion controls
questions.explanation: Input method can influence cybersickness: motion controls such as handlebars may cause more sickness than non-motion controls like joysticks, and a gamepad can cause less than a hand controller.

data.text: VR cybersickness can arise from external hardware factors, not only from poor hardware quality. Device characteristics matter: resolution helps only up to a point, while latency and its jitter can increase discomfort. The display and input method also influence severity, with headsets and motion controls sometimes increasing it, though higher-end HMDs and gamepads can reduce it.
points: Hardware is an external, not user-dependent VR cybersickness factor, and device aspects, rather than only poor quality, can induce it.
VR display resolution reduces cybersickness substantially from 1K to 2K, but little further from 2K onward.
VR latency is the delay between physical movement and virtual update, and higher latency increases cybersickness.
Latency jitter is changing latency; it disrupts timing and can cause discomfort, disorientation, and cybersickness.
Display type and input method affect cybersickness; headsets and motion controls can raise it, higher-end HMDs and gamepads lower it.

questions.question: Where does virtual reality content sit in the classification of cybersickness causes?
options: As an external factor
As a subjective factor
As an internal factor
As a hardware factor
questions.explanation: Virtual reality content is an external cause of cybersickness, separate from internal personal causes and from hardware causes such as display type and latency. It is not classified as internal or subjective, and it is not itself a hardware factor.

questions.question: Which pair of factors is counted as internal rather than external in cybersickness causes?
options: Input technology and display type
Age and gender
Display type and latency
Latency jitter and resolution
questions.explanation: Age and gender are internal personal factors in the causes of cybersickness. The other pairs are hardware factors, which are external rather than internal.

data.text: Cybersickness causes are broadly grouped into internal user factors and external factors. Internal factors include age and gender, while external hardware factors include display, latency, and input technology. VR content is another external cause, following the internal and hardware causes.
points: Cybersickness causes include internal factors such as age and gender, and external hardware factors such as display, latency, and input.
VR content is another external factor among the causes of cybersickness.

items.reason: Nausea, dizziness and headache are symptoms that may indicate the onset of cybersickness; anxiety is a negative emotion that can increase the likelihood of cybersickness.

items.reason: Age, gender and physical condition are internal factors for cybersickness; display type is a hardware factor.

items.reason: Brightness, clarity and contrast are display qualities of a head-mounted display; latency is the time delay between a user's physical movement and the corresponding virtual change.

questions.question: Why might a wider inter-pupillary distance adjustable range in virtual reality displays be especially useful for female users of head-mounted displays?
questions.reference_answer: A wider inter-pupillary distance adjustable range may be especially useful for female head-mounted display users because they are associated with increased cybersickness, and a possible reason is trouble finding a good inter-pupillary distance fit. Inter-pupillary distance determines stereoscopic vision. A wider adjustable range can therefore help female users achieve a better fit.

questions.question: Why can latency jitter be an additional cybersickness risk in head-mounted display virtual reality beyond the risk created by latency itself?
questions.reference_answer: Latency jitter can add risk on top of latency itself because it makes latency vary from time to time, causing irregularities in the timing of data delivery. In head-mounted display virtual reality, cybersickness increases with latency. Latency is the time gap between a user's movement and the corresponding change in the virtual world. Those irregularities can lead to inconsistencies, discomfort, disorientation, and cybersickness.

questions.question: Why can a high-end head-mounted display still produce more cybersickness than a conventional monitor, even though it produces less than a lower-end head-mounted display?
questions.reference_answer: Display type significantly influences cybersickness severity, and head-mounted display users experience more cybersickness than users of conventional monitors or non-immersive virtual reality systems. Within head-mounted displays, higher-end models cause less cybersickness than lower-end models because of better resolution, brightness, clarity, and contrast. A high-end head-mounted display can therefore reduce some hardware-quality effects while still being a more sickness-inducing display type than a monitor.
